hero.subtitle: A local MCP server that indexes your codebase and lets any AI assistant search it with paths, line ranges, and semantic understanding. Your code stays on your machine.

features.title: Everything You Need to Index & Search
features.subtitle: From chunking to embeddings to hybrid search — all in one MCP server.

items.title: Hybrid Search
items.desc: Combine keyword (FTS5 + BM25) with semantic search (Qdrant embeddings) via Reciprocal Rank Fusion for the best results.

items.title: Local-First Storage
items.desc: SQLite for metadata + FTS, Qdrant for vectors. All data stays on your machine — no cloud required.

items.title: Incremental Indexing
items.desc: SHA-256 file hashing skips unchanged files. Index once, re-index only what changed.

items.title: AI-Native
items.desc: Built for Model Context Protocol. Works with Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, Antigravity, and more.

items.title: 40+ Languages
items.desc: TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, C#, and more. Dependencies, symbols, exports — all indexed.

items.title: Smart Context
items.desc: Auto-detect frameworks, package managers, monorepos. Generate agent rules and project briefings.

install.title: Get Started in 2 Minutes
install.subtitle: Install dependencies, paste config, index your project, and search.

items.q: Do I need an API key?
items.a: No. vibe-hnindex runs entirely on your machine. Ollama provides local embeddings, and Qdrant stores vectors locally. No cloud API keys needed.

items.q: Can I use it without Qdrant?
items.a: Yes! Without Qdrant, vibe-hnindex falls back to keyword-only search (SQLite FTS5). Semantic and hybrid modes require Qdrant.

items.q: How is this different from Cursor's codebase indexing?
items.a: vibe-hnindex is IDE-agnostic — it works with any MCP-compatible assistant (Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, Antigravity, VS Code). You index once and search from any tool.
Yes! vibe-hnindex supports Windows, macOS, and Linux. On Windows, Node 20 or 22 LTS is recommended to avoid C++ compiler issues.
